1. **Implemented surface**: read `runtime/linux/syscall.c`, `mm.c`, `loader.c`, `stack.c`, `main.c`, `manifest.h`, `vlinux_mem.h`. List EVERY Linux syscall number/name that is handled (and what it does — real, stubbed, or -ENOSYS), plus the other behaviors (manifest parsing, auxv entries built, brk/mmap arena bounds, ELF loader checks, error paths).

2. **Existing tests**: list every file under `tests/vlinux/` and `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh`, and for each say exactly what it asserts, which andesim mode(s) it runs (fast/cycle/hybrid), and which engine it uses. Also list the `tests/fixtures/rt_linux_*.c` fixtures and what each exercises.

3. **Wiring**: is each vlinux test actually run by `scripts/test_all.sh` and/or `scripts/run_e2e.sh`? Quote the relevant lists/arrays. Are any vlinux tests orphaned (exist on disk but never invoked by any runner)?

5. **Gaps**: name concretely which implemented syscalls/behaviors have NO test at all, and which modes (fast/cycle/hybrid) are untested for the linux runtime.

Do not modify anything. Report as a compact structured list with file:line references.

23	 * every read back to the empty-string initializer below and vlinux never
24	 * notices a manifested app_path. */
25	__attribute__((section(".manifest"), used)) const volatile struct
26	  vlinux_manifest g_manifest = {
27	    .magic = VLINUX_MANIFEST_MAGIC,
28	    .version = VLINUX_MANIFEST_VERSION,
29	    .mem_size = 1024ull * 1024 * 1024,
30	    .app_path = "",

34	/* Set sp and jump to the app's entry point. Never returns -- the app runs
35	 * with vlinux's own C stack gone, so there is nothing left to return to. */
36	static void __attribute__((noreturn)) enter_app(uintptr_t sp, uintptr_t entry)
37	{
38	  /* load_elf() wrote the app's code via ordinary guest stores (through the
39	   * D-cache crt0.S enabled); without fence.i those writes are not
40	   * guaranteed visible to instruction fetch -- on a real cached core (unlike
41	   * QEMU's cacheless functional model, where this was silently a no-op) the
42	   * hart can fetch stale/empty I-cache lines instead of the just-written
43	   * code. Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes then executes
44	   * new code, not a workaround for this engine specifically. */
45	  asm volatile("fence.i\n"
46	               "mv sp, %0\n"
47	               "jr %1\n"
48	               :
49	               : "r"(sp), "r"(entry)
50	               : "memory");
51	  for (;;)
52	    ; /* unreachable */
53	}

11	 * v2 (U8): adds argv[1..] -- the app's own argv[0] is always app_path, so
12	 * only the EXTRA args from the user's `-- <args...>` need carrying. Flat
13	 * NUL-separated buffer + count (the same shape Linux's own argv/envp/auxv

15	 * `llama-completion -- -m model.gguf -no-cnv --prompt "..." -n 32 -t 1`

#ifndef VLINUX_MANIFEST_H
#define VLINUX_MANIFEST_H

#include <stdint.h>

/* .manifest section wire format (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U1/U2/U8). This
 * default instance ships inside vlinux.elf as built; the driver's
 * `objcopy --update-section .manifest=<blob>` overwrites it per run with
 * the real app_path/mem_size/argv.
 *
 * v2 (U8): adds argv[1..] -- the app's own argv[0] is always app_path, so
 * only the EXTRA args from the user's `-- <args...>` need carrying. Flat
 * NUL-separated buffer + count (the same shape Linux's own argv/envp/auxv
 * block uses), not one fixed-size slot per arg: a real invocation like
 * `llama-completion -- -m model.gguf -no-cnv --prompt "..." -n 32 -t 1`
 * has a handful of args of very different lengths, and a flat buffer
 * wastes no space on padding a slot to the longest possible arg.
 *
 * v3 (U10d): adds ram_base. Guest RAM is [ram_base, ram_base + mem_size);
 * vlinux derives every bound from that pair via vlinux_mem.h instead of
 * treating mem_size as an absolute address. ram_base == 0 reproduces v2's
 * layout exactly, and that is what the driver still sends today; a non-zero
 * base is what lets a >2 GiB guest live in QEMU AE350's DRAM_ALIAS/DRAM_EXT
 * window (0x8_00000000, contiguous for 16 GiB). The field was APPENDED, so a
 * v2 reader would mis-parse everything after it -- hence the version bump. */
#define VLINUX_MANIFEST_MAGIC   0x584c4e56u /* "VNLX" */
#define VLINUX_MANIFEST_VERSION 3u

#define VLINUX_MANIFEST_ARGV_BYTES 4096u    /* argv[1..] NUL-separated, total bytes */
#define VLINUX_MANIFEST_ARGV_MAX_COUNT 64u  /* argv[1..] entry count ceiling */

struct vlinux_manifest {
  uint32_t magic;
  uint32_t version;
  uint64_t mem_size;
  char     app_path[256];
  uint32_t argv_extra_count; /* number of EXTRA args (argv[1..]); 0 = none */
  uint32_t argv_extra_len;   /* bytes actually used in argv_extra_buf */
  char     argv_extra_buf[VLINUX_MANIFEST_ARGV_BYTES];
  uint64_t ram_base;         /* v3: guest RAM's first byte; 0 == v2 layout */
};

#endif /* VLINUX_MANIFEST_H */

8	/* Guest-RAM address math, in ONE place (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U10c).
9	 *
10	 * Guest RAM is the half-open range [ram_base, ram_base + mem_size). mm.c,
11	 * stack.c and loader.c each used to derive their bounds from `mem_size` alone
12	 * -- correct only while ram_base == 0. These three functions take the base
13	 * explicitly so a guest placed anywhere (e.g. QEMU AE350's DRAM_ALIAS at
14	 * 0x8_00000000, where the aliased low 2 GiB runs contiguously into DRAM_EXT)
15	 * computes the same layout. Pure, header-only, host-testable:
16	 * driver/vlinux_mem_test.cpp.
17	 *
18	 * The layout, from the top of RAM down:
19	 *   ram_top          -- one past the last RAM byte; the initial stack is built
20	 *                       growing DOWN from here (stack.c)
21	 *   v_scratch_base   -- the hybrid V-register transport page, the top
22	 *                       HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES; never handed out (loader.c
23	 *                       rejects any PT_LOAD overlapping it)
24	 *   mmap_arena_top   -- ram_top - VLINUX_STACK_RESERVE: the mmap bump
25	 *                       allocator's ceiling, leaving the stack its headroom
26	 *                       above (mm.c)
27	 * VLINUX_STACK_RESERVE lives here rather than in stack.h because mm.c and
28	 * stack.c MUST agree on it (see the comment this replaces); one definition,
29	 * one header, no way for them to desynchronize.
30	 */
31	#define VLINUX_STACK_RESERVE (8ull * 1024 * 1024)
32	
33	/* One past the last byte of guest RAM. */
34	static inline uint64_t vlinux_ram_top(uint64_t ram_base, uint64_t mem_size)
35	{
36	  return ram_base + mem_size;
37	}
38	
39	/* The mmap bump allocator's ceiling: below the app stack's reservation. */
40	static inline uint64_t vlinux_mmap_arena_top(uint64_t ram_base,
41	                                             uint64_t mem_size)
42	{
43	  return vlinux_ram_top(ram_base, mem_size) - VLINUX_STACK_RESERVE;
44	}
45	
46	/* First byte of the reserved hybrid V-transport scratch page. */
47	static inline uint64_t vlinux_v_scratch_base(uint64_t ram_base,
48	                                             uint64_t mem_size)
49	{
50	  return vlinux_ram_top(ram_base, mem_size) - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES;

1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
   3 # replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
   4 #
   5 # Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
   6 #   lint      tests/test_*.sh + roi.test.sh + the fixture ROI-content lint
   7 #             (fast harness self-checks; no engine spawns. The one heavy
   8 #             harness test, tests/test_kernel_cycles.sh, stays manual: it
   9 #             runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips the e2e phase already covers.)
  10 #   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
  11 #   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
  12 #   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
  13 #
  14 # Usage:
  15 #   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]
  16 #
  17 # --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
  18 # contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
  19 # first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
  20 set -uo pipefail
  21 
  22 ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
  23 
  24 DRY_RUN=0
  25 PHASES=()
  26 for arg in "$@"; do
  27   case "$arg" in
  28     --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
  29     lint|unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
  30     *)
  31       echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
  32       echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
  33       exit 2
  34       ;;
  35   esac
  36 done
  37 [ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(lint unit contract e2e)
  38 
  39 step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
   3 # (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
   4 #
   5 # Env overrides:
   6 #   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
   7 #   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
   8 #   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium,
   9 #                falling back to the first sim_* only when the canonical
  10 #                engine is not built -- see the comment at the default)
  11 #   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
  12 #   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
  13 #                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
  14 #                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
  15 #                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
  16 #   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
  17 #                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
  18 #                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
  19 #                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
  20 #                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
  21 #   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
  22 
  23 set -euo pipefail
  24 
  25 ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
  26 
  27 # Fill env gaps from ./config.env (the per-host file setup.sh maintains) so
  28 # `scripts/test_all.sh e2e` works from a fresh shell. An exported value wins;
  29 # the file only supplies what the caller's shell lacks -- same pattern as
  30 # tests/lib. Exported for the child builds (make -C tests/fixtures).
  31 cfg_val() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tail -1; }
  32 for _k in QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 \
  33           LINUX_TOOLCHAIN; do
  34   if [[ -z "${!_k:-}" ]]; then
  35     _v="$(cfg_val "$_k")"
  36     [[ -n "$_v" ]] && export "$_k=$_v"
  37   fi
  38 done
  39 unset _k _v
  40 
  41 # vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
  42 # VSIM_QEMU); empty when neither setup.sh nor config.env supplied it -- the
  43 # require below reports it.
  44 VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
  45 HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
  46 TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
  47 
  48 VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  49 VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  50 if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  51   # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  52   # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  53   # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
  54   # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  55   # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  56   # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  57   VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  58   if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
  59     VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  60   fi
  61 fi
  62 
  63 step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  64 ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  65 warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  66 fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
  67 
  68 require() {
  69   if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
  70     fail "$1 not found: $2"
  71     fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
  72     exit 1
  73   fi
  74 }
  75 require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
  76 require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
  77 require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
  78 
  79 export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
  80 
  81 # Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
  82 # e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
  83 # injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
  84 # NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
  85 RT_TESTS=(
  86   "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  87   "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  88   "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  89   "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  90   "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  91   "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  92   "rt_all_fprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_fprs"
  93   "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  94   "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  95   "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  96   "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
  97   "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
  98   "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  99   "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
 100   "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
 101   "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
 102   "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
 103   "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
 104   "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
 105   "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
 106   "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
 107   "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
 108   "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
 109   "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
 110   "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
 111 )
 112 
 113 NEG_TESTS=(
 114   "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
 115   "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
 116   "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
 117 )
 118 
 119 # Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
 120 # pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
 121 # (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
 122 # NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
 123 # ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
 124 # the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
 125 # lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
 126 # Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
 127 SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
 128   "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
 129   "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
 130 )
 131 
 132 # Fixture auto-build gate: the required ELF set is DERIVED from the test
 133 # tables above (each entry's FIXTURE= token), so it cannot drift from the
 134 # tests that consume the ELFs. The NEG_TESTS drivers reuse fixtures
 135 # already named in RT_TESTS (handoff_roundtrip, rt_c_dlm_data,
 136 # rt_c_hvm_data), so no separate list is needed for them.
 137 need_build=0
 138 for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}" "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
 139   fixture=""
 140   for tok in ${entry#*|}; do
 141     case "$tok" in FIXTURE=*) fixture="${tok#FIXTURE=}" ;; esac
 142   done
 143   if [[ -n "$fixture" && ! -e "$TEST_DIR/$fixture.elf" ]]; then
 144     need_build=1
 145   fi
 146 done
 147 if (( need_build )); then
 148   step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
 149   make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
 150 fi
 151 
 152 MODE="${MODE:-both}"
 153 case "$MODE" in
 154   marker|pc|both) ;;
 155   *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
 156 esac
 157 
 158 default_jobs() {
 159   local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
 160   n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
 161   if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
 162     shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
 163     if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
 164       shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
 165       (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
 166     fi
 167   fi
 168   (( n < 1 )) && n=1
 169   printf '%d\n' "$n"
 170 }
 171 JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
 172 [[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
 173   || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
 174 
 175 FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
 176 
 177 LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
 178 mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
 179 RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
 180 LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
 181 : > "$RESULTS_FILE"
 182 : > "$LOCK_FILE"
 183 
 184 # run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
 185 # Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
 186 # emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
 187 # (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
 188 # serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
 189 # children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
 190 # their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
 191 run_one() {
 192   local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
 193   local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
 194   local start end elapsed status rc
 195   start=$(date +%s)
 196   set +e
 197   bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
 198   rc=$?
 199   set -e
 200   end=$(date +%s)
 201   elapsed=$((end - start))
 202   case $rc in
 203     0)  status=PASS ;;
 204     77) status=SKIP ;;
 205     *)  status=FAIL ;;
 206   esac
 207   (
 208     flock 9
 209     case "$status" in
 210       PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
 211       SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
 212       FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
 213     esac
 214     printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
 215       "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
 216   ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
 217 }
 218 
 219 # Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
 220 # matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
 221 # the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
 222 declare -a WORKPLAN=()
 223 for tm in marker pc; do
 224   [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
 225   for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
 226     rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
 227     env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
 228     # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
 229     # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
 230     [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
 231     cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
 232     WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
 233   done
 234 done
 235 for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
 236   neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
 237   neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
 238   [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
 239   WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
 240 done
 241 
 242 # Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
 243 # after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
 244 declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
 245 for tm in marker pc; do
 246   [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
 247   for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
 248     rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
 249     env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
 250     [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
 251     cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
 252     SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
 253   done
 254 done

---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fixture ROI-content contract: a fixture whose phase-2 comment promises a
# kernel must actually carry that kernel BETWEEN the markers. The compiler
# may legally hoist an inlined kernel above enter_vsim() -- the markers'
# "memory" clobber does not cover statics whose address never escapes --
# which silently empties the ROI (rt_c_matmul shipped that way: markers
# back-to-back, window_cycles ~74 of pure drain overhead). Anchor rule
# (runtime/rt_c_helpers.h): kernels live in a noinline function called
# between the markers.
#
# Checks (static, objdump):
#   rt_c_matmul    span contains the GEMM: a kernel call (jal) or a mul
#   rt_c_v_matmul  span contains the kernel call (control: known-good)
#   rt_c_v_regs    span contains vector instructions (inline V kernel)
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[fixture_roi_content]: no objdump"; exit 77; }

FIXDIR="$SCRIPT_DIR"

# Instructions strictly between the ENTER and EXIT markers.
roi_body() {
  "$OBJDUMP" -d "$FIXDIR/$1.elf" \
    | awk '/5a002013/ { on = 1; next } /5a102013/ { exit } on'
}

check_roi() {  # $1 = fixture, $2 = required-content regex, $3 = description
  BODY=$(roi_body "$1")
  if [ -z "$BODY" ]; then
    fail "$1: ROI is EMPTY (markers back-to-back) -- kernel hoisted out?"
  fi
  if ! printf '%s\n' "$BODY" | grep -Eq "$2"; then
    echo "--- ROI body of $1 ---"
    printf '%s\n' "$BODY"

   6 # object already works at vlinux's load address (0x0200_0000) with no

#ifndef VLINUX_MM_H
#define VLINUX_MM_H

#include <stdint.h>

/* Set the brk arena's floor (the app's own image end -- loaded_elf.image_end)
 * and the mmap arena's ceiling (vlinux_mem.h's vlinux_mmap_arena_top --
 * "just below the app stack", the roadmap's guest memory map). Guest RAM is
 * [ram_base, ram_base + mem_size); pass ram_base 0 for the historical
 * flat-from-zero map. Must be called once, before any sys_brk/sys_mmap. */
void mm_init(uint64_t app_image_end, uint64_t ram_base, uint64_t mem_size);

/* The manifest's guest RAM size, for sys_sysinfo's totalram/freeram. */
uint64_t mm_total_ram(void);

/* brk(2): addr==0 queries the current break; otherwise tries to set it.
 * Linux syscall convention: always returns the RESULTING break (old value
 * on failure, not -1) -- glibc's brk() wrapper compares it against what it
 * asked for. */
long sys_brk(unsigned long addr);

/* mmap(2): bump-allocates from the top of the mmap arena downward.
 * MAP_ANONYMOUS is zeroed (the POSIX guarantee); `addr` is ignored (no
 * MAP_FIXED support). MAP_PRIVATE file-backed (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md
 * U7, llama.cpp's default GGUF load path): the [offset, offset+length)
 * range is eagerly read (htif_pread) into the freshly-allocated arena
 * space -- a real, private, independently-owned COPY, which is exactly
 * what MAP_PRIVATE promises (writes never propagate back to the file;
 * there is simply nowhere for this relay to route them even if it wanted
 * to). Read-only MAP_SHARED (PROT_WRITE clear) is accepted the same way
 * -- llama.cpp maps GGUF files MAP_SHARED + PROT_READ -- since a mapping
 * nothing writes through is observably identical to MAP_PRIVATE; only a
 * WRITABLE MAP_SHARED request is refused (-ENOSYS), because this relay
 * has no way to write a shared mapping's changes back to the host file.
 * Returns a negative errno on failure, matching the raw syscall (not the
 * libc wrapper's -1 + errno) convention. */
long sys_mmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot,
             long flags, long fd, long offset);

/* munmap(2)/mprotect(2): the bump allocator never reclaims or changes
 * protection (there is no MMU here -- every page is already RWX), so both
 * are accepted no-ops for ANY address/length, mapped or not -- POSIX
 * itself allows this (munmap(2): "it is not an error if the indicated
 * range does not contain any mapped pages"), so llama.cpp's partial
 * unmap of an unused GGUF tail range is answered correctly without
 * needing to track individual mappings. A real munmap would let the
 * arena run out sooner than it should; that is a leak, not a crash. */
long sys_munmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length);
long sys_mprotect(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot);

/* mremap(2): always refused (-ENOMEM, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U7) -- the
 * bump allocator has no in-place-grow or relocate-and-copy capability, so
 * a caller (llama.cpp does not use this for GGUF loading) gets a loud,
 * correct failure instead of silent corruption. */
long sys_mremap(unsigned long old_addr, unsigned long old_size,
                unsigned long new_size, unsigned long flags);
